wholesale_asking.label: Wholesale asking rent
wholesale_asking.text: The monthly price a landlord quotes for a block of capacity before negotiation, per kilowatt of IT load. Brokers publish it. It covers space, cooling and the critical power infrastructure. The electricity itself is usually billed separately at or near cost, and each row says whether its source stated that.

passing.label: Passing rent
passing.text: What a landlord actually collects today across signed leases of every vintage. We publish it only where the owner states the figure itself, in a prospectus, a circular or an earnings call. In a rising market it sits below asking rent, and the gap is the landlord's reversion. We never derive it ourselves from revenue and capacity, because the denominator cannot be audited by a reader.

retail_rack.label: Retail rack price
retail_rack.text: A published monthly list price for one rack with a stated power allowance, or a broker band for deployments under 250 kW. It bundles power and often bandwidth. Per kilowatt of allowance it is the highest of the three and it must never be compared with a wholesale figure. Racks under 3 kW are excluded because their price mostly measures fixed overhead.

bands.text: Block size changes the price more than the city does, so every figure carries its band. Retail is below 250 kW. Wholesale is 250 kW to 4 MW. Hyperscale is 4 MW and above. datacenterHawk and Cushman & Wakefield India draw the lines at 250 kW and 4 MW. CBRE prices a narrow 250 to 500 kW block. DC Byte's Singapore range covers all sizes. Figures from different bands are never averaged or compared as one series.

coverage.text: Two of the 34 markets on the map have a published colocation price we can stand behind, Singapore and India at national level. Every other market was searched through six channels, listed below, and returned nothing that survives review. An empty cell means nobody publishes the figure. It never means the market is cheap or free.

channels_searched: Stock exchange filings that republish commissioned market research (SGX REIT circulars and prospectuses, Indian draft prospectuses, bond documents)
Owner disclosures of in-place rent (prospectus reversion analyses, earnings calls)
Broker reports and press releases (CBRE, Cushman & Wakefield, JLL, Colliers, Knight Frank)
Government procurement records and published tariffs
Equity research made public and financial press quoting it

review.text: A practitioner review on 30 September 2026 graded 96 candidate figures. 21 survived, 42 are held pending verification and 33 were rejected. The held and rejected figures are listed at the foot of the page with the reason for each, so a reader can see what was left out and why.

meta.not_shown: No modelled cost floor is shown yet. A floor needs a sourced build cost per market, which exists for four markets today. It will be added as a separately labelled band once the construction cost tables for every covered market have been read.

estimate.text: The ArusGrid estimate is a fourth figure, kept apart from the three observed classes. It is computed by fixed rules from stated inputs, never typed in, shown only as a range with its grade and its inputs, and never counted in any total. It applies only to wholesale and hyperscale colocation; own-use builds, powered shells, retail and interconnection houses and GPU cloud get no price. Grade A or B is an observed figure for the building. Grade B is also the published band for the building's own country with a binding cost floor from the building's stated capex at a sourced yield on cost. Grade C is the band alone. Grade D is withheld: the regional fallback, a range wider than half its midpoint, or a floor that contradicts the band.
estimate.calibration_text: Every building with an independent observed figure is also estimated blind, one row per source document, excluding any figure that set a parameter or built a band, and the midpoint error is printed. The log starts on 1 October 2026.
